events.name: A Stair That Wasn't Here
events.intro: A stairway down that wasn't here a moment ago. The rooms below change every time. A Bidoof in an explorer's scarf sits on the top step. Bidoof (subtitled): "You're going down? Take a scarf. Everyone needs a scarf." Bidoof: "The only way out is through. Or back up, before it's too late."

success.text: The stair is longer than it looks. The light behind you gets small. You have 3 Luck.
The Bidoof ties it round your lead's neck with great care. It's just a scarf. You feel luckier anyway: 4 Luck.
You step back. When you look again, the stair is gone.

events.name: The Item Room
events.intro: A pedestal. One item. A sign: "TAKE ONE."

success.text: You take it. Nothing happens. You were braced for something.
You leave it on the pedestal. Somewhere, the dungeon seems to approve. The dungeon likes manners. +1 Luck.
A second item, tucked underneath. And a click. A trap snaps shut an inch from your fingers. -1 Luck.

events.name: The Monster House
events.intro: A room full of sleeping Pokémon. A stair on the far side. Every step is a gamble.

success.text: One step. Another. Nobody stirs. You reach the stair and breathe out.

failure.text: A floorboard creaks. Every eye in the room opens at once.

success.text: You clap your hands. The whole room wakes up angry.

choices.label: Throw a Berry to the corner.

success.text: The Berry lands in the corner. Every sleeper wakes, sniffs, and runs for it. You walk through the middle of the room and nobody looks at you.

events.name: The Trap Corridor
events.intro: A floor that clicks. Some tiles are clearly safe. Some aren't.

success.text: Dust means nobody has set them off, and they're stable. You cross without a sound.
Clean means somebody set them off, often. Click. Something swings past your ear. -1 Luck.
It goes first, carefully. A dart catches it on the way, but it waves you across.

events.name: The Fork
events.intro: Three ways, each marked by a smell: smoke, salt, flowers.

success.text: A room full of embers, and a Charcoal on a ledge. Something hot guards it.
A cool pool of sea water, far underground. You rest your feet in it. +1 Luck.
A room of Berry bushes growing in the dark. You pick three.

events.name: Kecleon's Shop
events.intro: A shop in the middle of nowhere, run by a Kecleon who never changes colour. Kecleon: "Welcome! Fair prices, fixed prices, no haggling, no stealing. Stealing makes me cross."

success.text: Every price is printed, and every one is fair. Kecleon watches you shop with great approval.
Kecleon: "Customers like to know where I am." It beams at you.
You pocket something. Kecleon's eyes swivel. Then it grows, and grows, until it fills the shop.

events.name: An Empty Room
events.intro: Where Kecleon's shop was, an empty room. A single sign on the wall: "NO."

success.text: You walk on. You can feel it watching you from somewhere.

events.name: The Sleeping Den
events.intro: Something asleep on a pile of treasure: a Snorlax.

success.text: One Nugget, lifted very, very slowly. The Snorlax snores on.
Three Nuggets, and the pile shifts. One eye opens. Then the other.
You let it sleep. It smiles in its sleep. +1 Luck.

events.name: The Ambush
events.intro: A hall that smells of many Pokémon. The doors lock behind you.

success.text: They come at you from every side. Three fights, back to back.
You feel along the wall for a long time. A stone gives. A hidden door, and a scrape on your arm. -1 Luck.
You stand still. They come one at a time, unsure of you. Easier. Slower.

events.name: The Boss Door
events.intro: A big door, a bigger lock, and the sound of something heavy on the other side.

success.text: The door swings in. The floor's boss turns to look at you.
You knock. The door opens by itself. The boss inside is curious, not angry.
A long way round, past the door and its treasure. The air gets fresher.

events.name: The Spring
events.intro: A spring at the bottom, glowing softly. An exit stair on the far side. The Bidoof is waiting. Bidoof: "You made it! Drink! Everybody drinks!"

success.text: Cold and bright. Your whole team drinks, and every ache goes out of them.
You fill a bottle. It glows in your bag all the way up the stairs.
You nod to the Bidoof and climb. Explorers know when to go.

remembers.notice: The Bidoof takes off its own scarf and holds it out to you. Bidoof: "You're a real explorer now."

events.name: The Cursed Idol
events.intro: A small golden idol on a pedestal in a ruin. The air around it is wrong. Carved on the pedestal: "IT PAYS. IT KEEPS COUNT."

success.text: It's heavier than gold should be. Somewhere, very faintly, something starts counting.
Under the first line, smaller, worn almost smooth: "IT WANTS TO GO HOME."
You leave it where it is. The air feels better the further you walk.

remembers.notice: Your Ghost-type turns its back on the idol and will not look at it.

events.name: The Cursed Idol
events.intro: IT PAYS. IT KEEPS COUNT. IT WANTS TO GO HOME.

success.text: It's heavier than gold should be. Somewhere, very faintly, something starts counting.
You leave it. It's been waiting this long.

events.name: Its Shrine
events.intro: The idol is heavy in your bag. A small shrine on the road has a pedestal the exact size of it. A child is sweeping the shrine. She looks at your bag. Child, Suki: "Oh. You found it. Grandma said somebody would bring it back one day."

success.text: You set it on the pedestal. The counting stops. The curse lifts all at once, like a held breath let go. The money stays. Suki's grandma comes out with a Cleanse Tag and presses it into your hand.
Suki nods like she expected that. "It'll come back here," she says. "They always do." The idol feels heavier already.
Suki: "A man took it to pay a debt. He died rich and alone." She leans on her broom and waits.

remembers.notice: The face in every reflection, all this time: Suki's grandfather. When the idol touches the pedestal you see him once more, in the shrine's bell, smiling.

events.name: Its Shrine
events.intro: Suki waits, broom in hand.

success.text: You set it on the pedestal. The counting stops. The curse lifts all at once. The money stays. Suki's grandma gives you a Cleanse Tag.
Suki: "Rich and alone," she says again, quietly. The idol feels heavier.

events.name: A Torn Page
events.intro: A page drifts across the road, covered in old handwriting. It's about a trainer with a {starter}. "...and the trainer stopped at the bridge, though nobody asked them to..."

success.text: You fold it carefully and put it somewhere it won't crease.
The wind takes it over the hedge. You have a feeling you'll see it again.

events.name: A Torn Page
events.intro: A region later, the same page catches on your boot. "...and the trainer stopped at the bridge, though nobody asked them to..."

success.text: You keep it. It seems to have come a long way to find you.
You let it go. Some pages want to wander.

events.name: A Torn Page
events.intro: Another page, the same old hand. "...the second time, the trainer chose differently, and the Pokémon noticed..."

success.text: You keep it.

choices.label: Write a note on the back: "Thank you."

success.text: You write it small, in the corner. It looks like it belongs there.

choices.label: Write a note on the back: "Keep going."

success.text: You write it small, in the corner. It looks like it belongs there.

events.name: A Torn Page
events.intro: The last page you find. "...and at the end, nobody remembered the battles. They remembered the—" It's torn there.

success.text: You keep it, and the missing word stays missing.
You hold the page and think about it for a long time.

events.name: A Torn Page
events.intro: "They remembered the—"

success.text: You write it in pencil, lightly, so it can be rubbed out.
You write it in pencil, lightly, so it can be rubbed out.
You write it in pencil, lightly, so it can be rubbed out.

events.name: The Collector
events.intro: A scholar spots the pages in your hand and gasps. Archivist Hume: "Those belong together! I've been looking for thirty years." Hume: "It's a story told on this road for a century. Every teller changes it. These are the oldest pages anyone's found."

success.text: Hume reads them aloud, right there on the road. Halfway through he stops. "The old woman. The Storyteller. She's in it, by name." His hands shake. "Then her road is real."

You read them side by side. The trainer at the bridge. The second choice. And the end: "...nobody remembered the battles. They remembered the kindness." Hume: "The Storyteller's road. It starts further along than I thought."
Hume understands. He copies them by hand, slowly, while you wait. In the margin of his copy he draws a small pink shape, without knowing why.

remembers.notice: Hume sees your pencilled word and goes very still. "That's it. That's exactly what it says."
Hume reads your pencilled word. "That's not what it says." A pause. "But it should be." He writes your word in, beside the old one.
On the back of the second page, in your own handwriting: your note. Hume reads it out too, as if it was always part of the story.

events.name: The Great Berry Festival
events.intro: Bunting, music, the smell of a thousand Berries. A banner: THE GREAT BERRY FESTIVAL. Festival mayor, Pudding: "Welcome, welcome! Taste everything! Well. Taste what there is." Half the stalls are empty.

success.text: Pudding's smile slips.
Small, sour, and wonderful. Your team eats until they can't. Pudding presses one more Berry into your hand for the road.
Pudding points you to a big tent with a hand-painted sign.

remembers.notice: An old seed packet on Pudding's table, faded: ABNER'S SEEDS. Pudding: "He bought his first seeds here. Decades ago."

events.name: The Shortage
events.intro: Pudding: "A drought hit the orchards. The grove behind the grounds is all we've got left, and something's living in it."

success.text: Pudding: "Bless you. Bless you. Mind the roots."
One stall, two, five. The empty tables fill up one by one, and people start to come back to them. Pudding cries a little, then hands you something rare from her own pocket.
Pudding: "The spring under the Guardian Tree dried up. Nobody knows why." She looks up the hill. "Nobody's been up there in years."

events.name: The Thief
events.intro: A Pokémon bolts from a stall, cheeks stuffed with Berries. The vendor wails. It's a Skwovet, very thin. It runs toward the grove.

success.text: You follow it through the stalls and over a fence. It leads you into the grove, to a hollow in the roots. Its family is there, starving.
You pay. The vendor is so grateful she hugs you. Later, on the road, a thin Skwovet steps out of the hedge and leaves a Berry at your feet.
You let it go. It looked so thin.

events.name: The Grove
events.intro: Behind the festival, Berry trees grow wild and heavy. Something nests in the roots: a family of Skwovet and Greedent, hoarding everything. Their own grove up the hill dried up.

success.text: You sit down between the festival and the family and work it out: half the trees for the stalls, half for them. The Greedent thinks about it, and then nods, once.
The Greedent puffs up to twice its size and comes at you.

choices.label: Find out why their grove dried.

success.text: The smallest Skwovet tugs your sleeve and leads you up the hill.

events.name: The Merchant
events.intro: A wagon of rare Berries from far regions. Berry merchant, Sabba: "Never tasted anything like them, friend. Kee, Maranga, Roseli. Fair prices."

success.text: Sabba spreads them out, each with its price on a little card.
You buy a basket and carry it straight to the contest tent. The judges add a whole new category: Rare Berries.
Sabba names the regions on her fingers. The last one she names is {nextRegion}. "You'll see," she says. "They grow them big there."

events.name: The Merchant
events.intro: Kee Berry, ₽400. Maranga Berry, ₽400. Roseli Berry, ₽300. Fair prices, printed.

success.text: Sabba wraps it in a leaf.
Sabba wraps it in a leaf.
Sabba wraps it in a leaf.
Sabba waves. "Next region, friend."

events.name: The Contest
events.intro: Judges grade Berries on size, flavour and shine. Judge Plumridge: "Enter one Berry. We'll know if it's bought or grown."

success.text: Plumridge turns it over twice. "Middling. Honest, though." A small prize: a ribbon and a bag of seeds.
Plumridge holds it up to the light for a long time. "Grown. With care." First prize: a Berry Pouch, and your name on the board.
You watch. An old man wins with a Berry the size of his head. Everyone cheers.

remembers.notice: A new table at the end of the tent, under a new sign: RARE BERRIES. Your donation, sorted and labelled.

success.text: Plumridge turns it over. "Middling. But the Rare table needs entries." Second prize in the new category: a Starf Berry.

events.name: The Guardian Tree
events.intro: A great old Berry tree. A Pokémon in its branches watches you with calm eyes: a Tsareena. The spring at its roots is dry. A stone has fallen into it, wedged tight.

success.text: Your Pokémon sets its feet and heaves. The stone grinds, rocks, and rolls clear. Water bubbles up, then runs. The Tsareena comes down from the branches and touches your Pokémon's head.
The Tsareena looks at you, then points one long leg at the stone.
Your Water-type fills the spring at every node you pass. It holds. For a region, at least.

events.name: The Guardian Tree
events.intro: The Tsareena points at the stone. Then it waits.

success.text: The stone grinds, rocks, and rolls clear. Water bubbles up. The Tsareena comes down from the branches.
The Tsareena goes back to watching.

events.name: The Seedling
events.intro: Botanists compare mutations under glass. One offers you a seedling in a pot. Botanist, Dr. Fennimore: "Would you grow this? It needs a trainer's care. Talk to it." Fennimore: "It's a new Berry. It'll be named after whoever grows it."

success.text: You take the pot. It's very small. You water it at every rest, and talk to it when nobody's looking. (It fruits after 4 rests.)
Fennimore: "We don't know yet. That's the fun."
Fennimore nods and puts the pot back under the glass.

events.name: The Seedling Fruits
events.intro: Your seedling has fruited: one Berry, a colour nobody has a name for yet. The festival's contest is still on.

success.text: You carry it all the way back with both hands.
You keep it. It's yours. You grew it.

events.name: The Festival, Full
events.intro: Next region, the festival again: every stall stocked, the spring running, the Greedent family asleep on a full larder. On a new board by the gate, a new Berry, and your name on it.

success.text: Everything. Pudding refuses your money.

events.name: The Raid
events.intro: In the night, something big gets into your bag. In the morning: a Greedent, very fat, waddling away into the trees. It looks back once. It remembers you.

success.text: Your Berries are gone. Most of them.

events.name: Behind the Curtain
events.intro: A curtain parts. Goods no shop would sell. Dealer, Silk: "Everything's half price. Everything's stolen. I'm honest about that."

success.text: Silk wraps it in newspaper. Somewhere, the evil team's next plan gets a little closer.
Silk: "Trainers who didn't lock their bags."
Silk sighs. "Fair." Officers come for her before the stage is out. One of them writes down what you saw: a lead on the Smuggling Ring.

events.name: Questionable Bargains
events.intro: A street stall. Vendor: "Cheap, cheap! Don't ask where it came from."

success.text: He wraps it fast and looks over his shoulder twice.
Vendor (very quietly): "...A Rocket fella. Don't tell him I said." You have a name for the owner now.
You walk on.

events.name: The Crate
events.intro: A smuggler pats a stencilled crate. "Unopened. May include a banned item. No refunds." He shows you a card: Life Orb 20%. Eviolite 20%. Assault Vest 20%. Weakness Policy 20%. Muscle Band 20%. "I'm a smuggler, not a liar."

success.text: You pry the lid off.
He puts a hand flat on the lid. "No refunds means no peeking." Then he waits.
The officers open it. Inside, wrapped in a towel: one Poké Ball, scratched, with a name on it. It goes back to its owner through the Lost and Found. You never see their face, but you hear about it.

events.name: The Crate
events.intro: The card again: Life Orb 20%. Eviolite 20%. Assault Vest 20%. Weakness Policy 20%. Muscle Band 20%.

success.text: You pry the lid off.
He shrugs. "Your loss. Twenty percent, each."

events.name: Want Something Nobody Else Has?
events.intro: An alley. A voice: "Want something nobody else has?" It's a rare held item: a Focus Sash. The tag says it was a Gym Leader's.

success.text: You buy it. It's a good item. The tag is still on it.
The tag says it belonged to the {gymType} Leader. The voice laughs. "Not any more."

choices.label: I'll take it back to them.

success.text: "Over my body." The seller steps out of the dark.

events.name: That Was Ours
events.intro: A Grunt steps in front of you. Grunt: "That item you bought. It was ours. Hand it over."

success.text: He takes the Choice Band and walks off without a word.
Grunt: "Fine. The hard way."

choices.label: It was someone's before it was yours.

success.text: Grunt: "...Huh." You name the owner from the stall. He stares at you, then shrugs. "Fine. Give it back to them, then. Not my problem." You do.

events.name: The Estate Sale
events.intro: A house full of things, and a sign: EVERYTHING MUST GO. A relative in the doorway, arms crossed. Relative, Dora: "Take what you want. Prices are on the tags. Don't haggle. I can't today."

success.text: Fair prices, all of them low. You find a held item in a drawer of old ribbons.
Dora: "My uncle. He ran a Gym. Forty years ago. Nobody remembers." She looks at a small leather case on the mantel. "That's his badge case."
You leave her to it.

events.name: The Estate Sale
events.intro: Dora holds the badge case in both hands.

success.text: She lets it go slowly. Inside: eight old badges, and a photograph of a young man with a Machop on his shoulder.
You close her hands around it. Dora: "...Thank you. Nobody asked about him. Not once, all week."
She does. A small Gym, a Fighting Gym, forty years ago, where everybody knew everybody. She tells you his name. You won't forget it.
